name: What should I do if mold or water damage is found during a guest bathroom remodel?

mainEntity.name: What happens if mold, rot, or water damage is discovered after demo starts in a guest bathroom remodel?
mainEntity.text: What happens if mold, rot, or water damage is discovered after demo starts in a guest bathroom remodel?

acceptedAnswer.text: Hidden water damage is one of the most common reasons a guest bathroom remodel expands beyond the original scope. If mold, rot, or a wet subfloor is found after demolition, the damaged material should be removed and the source of moisture corrected before any new finish work begins. That may mean replacing subfloor sections, repairing framing, improving ventilation, or rebuilding parts of the shower assembly. In older homes around Los Angeles, Glendale, Pasadena, and Burbank, damage often comes from slow leaks that were hidden behind tile for years. The key is to fix the problem fully rather than cover it up. A good contractor should explain the issue clearly, document the damage, and show how the repair affects budget and schedule. This is exactly why a contingency allowance is smart on bathroom projects. If waterproofing or rot is ignored, the new remodel can fail quickly and become much more expensive later.
acceptedAnswer.description: If mold or water damage is found, the affected area should be opened, removed, dried, and repaired before new finishes go back in. The remodel may expand beyond the original plan if the subfloor, framing, or waterproofing system is compromised. Hidden damage usually adds cost and time.
